I really thought postpartum would mean I’d slowly just go back to the level of fitness I had before pregnancy.
But 5 minutes into the @evolvewindsor 5k, I started getting upper ab pain and realized my body is still healing in ways I can’t always see.
So I walked parts of it and slowed down. I met my body where it’s at right now instead of forcing it to be where it used to be, but was I frustrated… yes … and I still frustrated .. YES ! 
7 months postpartum has humbled me in a lot of ways, but it’s also teaching me to give myself more grace.
Showing up still counts. Even if it looks different than before.

#postpartum #postpartumfitnessjourney

I’m slowly learning that taking longer doesn’t mean something is wrong. It means my body, my heart, and my identity have been through something huge.
I’m learning to be patient with myself. To stop asking when I’ll “feel normal again” and start honoring everything it took to get here. 
This season has changed me, and maybe my spark isn’t gone…it’s just different. Quieter. Deeper. Still finding its way back.
If you’re in this space too, feeling like yourself feels far away, I want you to know you’re not behind and you’re not alone.

Everyone thinks their milk supply “dipped” around 8–12 weeks…

but most of the time, it didn’t. Your milk just regulated.

Soft boobs ≠ no milk.
No leaking ≠ low supply.
Pumping less ≠ failing.

Early postpartum your body overproduces just in case ( you know like me have twins ).

Then it gets smarter and starts making milk on demand.
Less drama. Less pain.
More sustainable.

If baby is gaining weight + having wet diapers, your body is doing exactly what it’s supposed to 🤍

caption:
21 weeks pregnant with twins… and honestly, I wasn’t sure if I could still work out.
Not just physically but mentally. I had so many doubts.

Would it be safe? 
Would I feel too tired?
Would I even feel like myself anymore?

At first, I let the fear keep me still. I thought if I couldn’t do things the way I used to, maybe I shouldn’t do them at all. 
But slowly, I realized movement didn’t have to disappear… it just had to change.

Now, working out looks different. It’s gentler, slower, more about listening to my body than pushing through. Some days, it’s a short walk. Some days, it’s a good sweat and a reminder that I’m still strong even while growing two little humans.

I’m not doing this to “bounce back” or prove anything. I’m doing it because it helps me feel good, stay grounded, and connect with myself in a season where so much is changing.

So if you’re pregnant and unsure if you can keep moving you can.
It won’t be the same, but it can still be powerful.
You’re not losing who you are… you’re just becoming a new version.
And she’s strong in a whole new way.

#pregnancy #pregnancyworkout #pregnancydiary #pregnancyisbeautiful #workout
